job: Folding a tool-executing agent loop into the general chat-and-tool-calls library as a documented first-class primitive rather than a separate framework.
outcome: A stock CodingAgent-style class and CLI callable in a few lines, with built-in filesystem and shell tools shipped in the library.
motivation: Keeps developers on their library as the agent loop commoditizes, and blocks rival libraries from claiming the built-in-agent default first.

task.where: the library's main repo and release
task.how: model-pluggable substrate, built-in file and shell tools

job: Shipping a few-hundred-line, vendor-decoupled, self-hostable permission-gated coding-agent loop atop a model-pluggable library to reset the ecosystem's reference shape.
outcome: A published `llm code` CLI and CodingAgent primitive whose minimal harness becomes the reference the mainstream libraries measure and copy.
motivation: Demonstrates the loop belongs in the base library, pressuring peers to adopt the same built-in shape instead of bespoke frameworks.

task.where: the llm library and its plugins

job: Designing the allowlist-and-approval-gate permission model that makes the built-in file-and-shell agent loop safe enough to ship as a default primitive.
outcome: A command allowlist or approval gate wired as the default safety control on the stock agent, so the loop ships enabled without a standalone dependency.
motivation: Without a credible default safety gate the loop cannot ship first-class, so gating work is the gating precondition for landing.

task.what: build allowlist and approval permission gate
task.why: make built-in file-and-shell tools shippable safely
task.how: command allowlist plus per-action approval gate
